text: I ought to be thy Adam, but I am rather the fallen angel, whom thou drivest from joy for no misdeed.
author: Mary Shelley

archive.text: I keep six honest serving-men (They taught me all I knew); their names are What and Why and When and How and Where and Who.
archive.author: Rudyard Kipling

archive.text: It's only when you look at an ant through a magnifying glass on a sunny day that you realise how often they burst into flames.
archive.author: Clive James

archive.text: When I am silent, I have thunder hidden inside.
archive.author: Rumi

archive.text: All problems of existence are essentially problems of harmony.
archive.author: Sri Aurobindo

archive.text: All men by nature desire to know.
archive.author: Aristotle

archive.text: A little knowledge that acts is worth infinitely more than much knowledge that is idle.
archive.author: Kahlil Gibran

archive.text: Every act of creation is first an act of destruction.
archive.author: Pablo Picasso
